_what: Every narration sentence maps to a span of script/essay.txt, the sources of record for this film.
essay_version: draft 1.1, 2026-10-24 (the 'itself, not itself' line ceded to the objecthood-transformations film, which closes on it)
thesis: CENTS is unfinished because its medium is the continual redefinition of value and meaning, carried out by its participants in time; the marks of circulation, the Council's names and Sets, the artist's death, the end of the penny, a museum show and the Void are each one more redefinition, and none closes the work.
epoch_convention: See essay [9]. Film speaks from 24 October 2026.

claims.say: Ten thousand copper cents, photographed, melted into a block, and inscribed on Bitcoin.
claims.span: He then archivally photographed them and cataloged each of their dates and mintages. Next, he removed them from circulation by melting them down into a solid copper block. Once destroyed, he inscribed each of the pennies as Bitcoin ordinals

claims.say: So where is the work?
claims.note: A rhetorical question that sets up the essay's claim about medium; asserts nothing.

claims.say: Not in the coins, which were melted, nor in any one image, nor in the block.
claims.span: its medium is the gesture of its continual becoming, rather than any of its visible manifestations

claims.say: Its medium is the gesture of its continual becoming, rather than any of its visible manifestations.
claims.span: its medium is the gesture of its continual becoming, rather than any of its visible manifestations

claims.say: A becoming does not arrive finished.
claims.span: CENTS is a becoming, a gesture that unfolds continually through the actions of its participants in time.
claims.epoch: not time-varying: a statement of the concept
claims.epoch_note: Flagged only because the span contains the project name CENTS, which the money detector reads as "cents".

claims.say: It unfolds continually, through the actions of its participants, in time.
claims.span: a gesture that unfolds continually through the actions of its participants in time
claims.note: Adapted (subject "It", added commas), so not tagged as a quotation.

claims.say: The cents left the mint identical, and decades of hands, pockets and air marked each one differently.
claims.span: Each of these objects, initially identical, bear the marks of touch and time.
claims.epoch: 1910-1982 mint years and the decades of circulation after

claims.say: So the piece is a kind of time-based generative art.
claims.span: the visual presence of the piece exists as time-based generative art

claims.say: In March 2024, Chang released the ten thousand inscriptions at one sat each, into indeterminate, continual revaluation.
claims.span: indeterminate, continual revaluation
claims.as_of: essay [1] 2025-10-30; release month from [7], project description 2024-03-26

claims.say: Then the participants began to read the set.
claims.span: I've witnessed collectors intricately dissect this set to determine its internal dynamics

claims.say: Over two years of voting, the Trait Council named what circulation had made: verdigris, obsidian, desert, ghost, fingerprints.
claims.span: The names came afterwards, from the collectors themselves, over two years of voting.
claims.as_of: house wording [6], approved by the user; knowledge brief 2026-10-24

claims.say: It defined Sets, ways of seeing the ten thousand as one structure.
claims.span: The Traits Council has defined a number of Sets.

claims.say: This is how a canon forms: words and phrases accrue significance as readers return to them.
claims.span: the way that individual words and phrases in texts accrue significance when they enter the scarce set of meanings referred to as “canon”

claims.say: Each reading redefines what a Cent is, and what it is worth.
claims.span: creating a situation where their value and meaning is indeterminate and continually redefined

claims.say: Rutherford Chang died in January 2025.
claims.span: Rutherford Chang died on 24 January 2025.

claims.say: That November, the last penny for general circulation was struck.
claims.span: The last penny produced for general circulation was minted at the U.S. Mint in Philadelphia on November 12, 2025.

claims.say: The work went on.
claims.note: Bridge sentence; the next sentence (UCCA, January 2026) is its evidence.

claims.say: In January 2026, CENTS was shown at UCCA Beijing, in the first institutional solo exhibition of Chang's work.
claims.span: the first institutional and most comprehensive solo exhibition of Rutherford Chang’s work

claims.say: Even loss is not an ending here.
claims.span: They are not lost but voided, and are monitored here in case one leaves that state.

claims.say: Some Cents have been swept, by wallets that do not track inscriptions, into vast shared holdings of bitcoin.
claims.span: each is bundled inside a large UTXO held by a wallet that does not track inscriptions

claims.say: They cannot be traded, but they are not destroyed.
claims.span: They cannot be listed, traded, or moved on their own.

claims.say: As of 24 October 2026, thirty-one have entered the Void, and none has been recovered.
claims.span: Derived: 31 Cents have entered the Void; none has been recovered

claims.say: Its meanings continue to emerge as participants co-create the intersubjective reality of its presence.
claims.span: Its meanings continue to emerge as participants co-create the intersubjective reality of its presence.
